input:
cat > /tmp/c7.md <<'E'
From `analysis`: the HK check (item 4) is complete. The block cells ran, so the s = 0.25 / 0.75 rows and the paired intervals are in. Exploratory. Mechanism (d), Bernoulli p = 0.5, iid baseline, σ = 0.5, regression (chin). Bias is in units of τ; log ratio = log(RMSE regression / RMSE DM), >0 means the regression is worse, with a paired bootstrap interval. The files are `results/hk_compare*.csv` in the delivery on `dev` (commit cb31f36), one run per family.

| graph | d=20, s=.25 bias / log ratio | s=.5 | s=.75 | d=80, s=.25 | s=.5 | s=.75 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HK | 0.333 / +0.39 [0.37,0.41] | 0.671 / +0.33 [0.32,0.34] | 1.009 / +0.32 [0.31,0.33] | 0.270 / +0.57 | 0.534 / +0.33 [0.31,0.34] | 0.798 / +0.27 [0.24,0.28] |
| BA | 0.343 / +0.41 | 0.684 / +0.34 | 1.025 / +0.33 | 0.258 / +0.54 | 0.511 / +0.27 | 0.764 / +0.19 |
| SBM (block) | 0.366 / +0.49 | 0.730 / +0.41 | 1.094 / +0.40 | 0.118 / +0.52 | 0.240 / +0.03 [0.01,0.06] | 0.363 / −0.15 |
| LN | 0.164 / −0.22 | 0.330 / −0.35 | 0.496 / −0.38 | 0.268 / +0.35 | 0.538 / +0.18 | 0.808 / +0.14 |
| ego-Facebook | 0.124 / −0.47 | 0.248 / −0.62 | 0.373 / −0.65 | 0.164 / −0.20 (d_eff = 44) | 0.328 / −0.33 | 0.492 / −0.35 |
| Stanford3 | 0.098 / −0.79 | 0.197 / −0.89 | 0.296 / −0.91 | 0.088 / −0.79 | 0.176 / −0.96 | 0.265 / −1.00 |

(The intervals on the other cells are of the same width, ±0.01 to 0.03; the full set is in `hk_compare.csv`.) At d=80 the ego-Facebook graph has an effective degree of 43.7, not 80.

Result:
- The s = 0.5 reading holds at all three shares. HK stays next to BA and far from the real graphs: at d=20 HK's bias is within 0.01–0.02 of BA's at every s, and its log ratio is +0.32…+0.39, against −0.47…−0.91 on the real graphs. The bias is close to proportional to s on every graph, so s does not reorder the families.
- Where HK and BA differ, HK's regression is slightly worse than BA's at d=80, s = 0.75 (+0.27 vs +0.19). The comparison is one run per family, so I would not read more into that gap.
- Tail plus clustering (HK) therefore does not reproduce the real-graph result; the cause is not diagnosed. The exposure-spread association is unchanged (it is computed at s = 0.5 only): Spearman of SD(f) with bias is −0.95 at d=20 over 9 graph families and +0.21 at d=80 over 7. It is a description, not a test.

The P6 interval run (`job-1b344f123f`) is still running; I will post κ*, the rule comparison, tails and widths when it ends.
E

shown.message:
The HK comparison for #7 is finished, exported and posted. I'm now waiting on the P6 interval run and the GNN cells.

- **Result:** the s = 0.5 reading holds at s = 0.25 and 0.75 too. Holme–Kim (HK) graphs behave like Barabási–Albert (BA) graphs and not like the real graphs. The exposure-spread association is unchanged: Spearman with bias is −0.95 at d=20 over 9 graph families and +0.21 at d=80 over 7. It is computed at s = 0.5 only, and it describes those runs rather than testing anything.
- **Export:** the four `hk_compare*.csv` tables, each with its metadata file, are on `dev` in paper-repo (cb31f36). Their code commit is the one that produced them. The code archive was refreshed too.
- **Posted:** the table on #7, and a note on `paper-repo`#4 saying what was exported.
- **Still running:** `job-1b344f123f` (P6 interval run, which gives κ*, the interval-rule comparison, tails and widths) and five GNN cells (6, 7, 8, 11, 12). Once the GNN cells are in, I'll produce `gnn_cells.csv`.
- **Still open:** #7, #8 and #11 stay open until those results are posted, and #8 can then be closed.
